record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.context_brief: Hit-or-miss and related interpretable template layers
record.original_question: For interpretable deep-learning template extraction, what formulation of the hit-or-miss transform gives learnable and robust template-extraction layers, how efficient is the integration of hit-or-miss layers into complex deep architectures, should such layers be limited to the first layers, how should pattern-detection equivariance be handled using group-morphology-based hit-or-miss transforms, and what other morphological template-extraction operators are relevant as interpretable deep-learning layers?

evidence.quote: What is the best formulation for the hit-or-miss transform to provide easy learnable and robust template extraction layers? How efficient is the integration of hit-or-miss layers into a complex architecture of deep learning? Only as the first layers? How to deal with equivariance in pattern detection by means of group morphology-based hit-or-miss transforms? What other morphological template extraction operators [62] are relevant as interpretable layers in deep learning?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let E be a discrete domain (e.g. E = Z^2) and let F(E, T) denote the set of functions f : E -> T with T an ordered set (e.g. T = R or T = {0,1}). For a structuring element B subset of E and f : E -> T, define the erosion (epsilon_B f)(x) = inf_{b in B} f(x+b) and the dilation (delta_B f)(x) = sup_{b in B} f(x+b). Given an ordered pair of disjoint structuring elements (B_fg, B_bg) (foreground and background templates), the classical (binary or grey-level) hit-or-miss transform of f is
   HMT_{(B_fg, B_bg)}(f)(x) = (epsilon_{B_fg} f)(x) - (delta_{B_bg} f)(x),
returning a measure of how well the pair (B_fg, B_bg) matches the local pattern of f near x. A hit-or-miss layer is a trainable parametrization (theta -> (B_fg(theta), B_bg(theta))) inserted into a deep neural network so that the templates (B_fg, B_bg) are learned end-to-end by gradient-based optimization.

For a topological group G acting on E, an operator Psi : F(E,T) -> F(E,T) is called G-equivariant if Psi(f circ g^{-1}) = Psi(f) circ g^{-1} for all g in G. Group-morphology-based hit-or-miss transforms are generalizations of HMT in which structuring elements and inf/sup operations are taken over orbits of G, so as to produce G-equivariant template-extraction operators.

Problem. Establish a theoretical and algorithmic framework for interpretable, learnable template-extraction layers based on the hit-or-miss transform. Specifically:
(1) Formulate the hit-or-miss transform (or a suitable relaxation/smoothing thereof) so that the resulting layer is differentiable with respect to the templates (B_fg, B_bg), robust to noise and small geometric perturbations of the input, and admits stable gradient-based training. Prove convergence and approximation guarantees for the proposed formulation.
(2) Determine the computational and statistical efficiency of integrating such hit-or-miss layers into deep architectures composed of standard linear, nonlinear, and pooling layers, and characterize whether their use is most effective only at early layers or also at intermediate/deep layers.
(3) For a given group G of geometric transformations of E (e.g. translations, rotations, scalings), construct group-morphology-based hit-or-miss transforms that are provably G-equivariant, and study their expressivity and trainability as deep-learning layers.
(4) Identify and analyze other morphological template-extraction operators (beyond the hit-or-miss transform) that yield interpretable trainable layers, and compare their approximation and invariance properties.
artifact.status_search_result: Hit-or-miss based deep layers have been studied in several recent works (e.g., Islam et al. on hit-or-miss CNN layers, Velasco-Forero and Angulo on morphological neural networks, and follow-up works on group-equivariant morphological operators), but no unified theoretical framework answering all the listed sub-questions is established. The questions on optimal formulation, placement in deep architectures, group-equivariance, and the catalog of useful morphological template operators remain active research directions without a definitive resolution.

status_evidence.title: Hit-or-Miss Transform with CNNs
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a learnable hit-or-miss transform layer for CNNs as an interpretable feature extractor.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on learnable HMT layers exists but does not resolve the broader open questions.

status_evidence.title: Group equivariant morphological neural networks
status_evidence.snippet: Recent works study equivariance for morphological layers, indicating the topic is ongoing.
status_evidence.claim: Group-equivariant morphological layers remain an active topic without complete answers.
